milestones: recognize that every coordinate token has two table-dependent readings
allow empty/filled provenance to vary per token rather than per row
construct at least two locally plausible five-letter candidates for each clue
select ALPHA GAMMA DELTA THETA SIGMA OMEGA through a cross-row Greek-letter ontology
preserve the stamp path used to spell each kept word instead of retaining only plaintext
infer ○=0 and ●=1 from the lock examples and decode six five-bit values
audit that both local clue fit and global-set membership are necessary

required_signals.signal: The two directories expose different letters at the same coordinates.
Each local clue admits two coherent words obtainable through opposite token choices.
One candidate from every row belongs to the Greek alphabet while the alternatives share no ontology.
Every label has five tokens and the lock has five holes with A/Z examples.

decoys.hypothesis: Choose one directory for an entire row or for the entire puzzle.
decoys.falsifier: Uniform-table readings are mostly gibberish and cannot satisfy all six clues; the flavor says the stamp of each coordinate token was lost.

decoys.hypothesis: Keep the more literal ordinary candidates FIRST, XRAYS, COAST, ANGLE, TOTAL, FINAL.
decoys.falsifier: Those words do not form a common standard set, and their complementary stamp paths produce values 29 and 27 on rows 1 and 4, outside A1Z26.

decoys.hypothesis: Treat a locally formed word such as the accidental all-filled GRAMS as sufficient.
decoys.falsifier: GRAMS does not satisfy the radiation clue and cannot join the cross-row Greek-letter ontology.

stamp color lost on the labels

coverage_ledger.element: five tokens and five lock holes

flavor_leak_rationale: The flavor establishes two possible token surfaces and a five-hole artifact but does not reveal either table, any candidate word, the Greek-letter ontology, the bit orientation, or the final values.

shortcut_red_team.shortcut: Decode every token with only one directory
shortcut_red_team.reason: Uniform readings do not satisfy all local clues; token-level mixing is necessary.

shortcut_red_team.shortcut: Guess the Greek words directly from the six clue descriptions
shortcut_red_team.reason: The final payload is the exact per-token stamp provenance and still requires all coordinate lookups.
They lack a common ontology and their complement paths fail the 1-26 checksum on two rows.
The A/Z examples fix orientation; inversion also creates out-of-range values.

shortcut_red_team.shortcut: Read coordinates or grid rows as an acrostic
shortcut_red_team.reason: Coordinates were deliberately permuted and yield no six-letter payload without branch provenance.

shortcut_red_team.shortcut: Use a same-letter pair to choose either stamp without consequence
shortcut_red_team.reason: Every target/alternative letter pair differs at every position, so each retained letter uniquely records a stamp choice.
